title: Unoverse object props
description: props.yaml: the object's OWN fields, one prop per key, every prop a brief (docs/unoverse/data/objects/README.md 4c). The prop grammar of UNOVERSE_AUTHORING.md 3b: description, type, input, limits as numbers, items on an array (the element's type, or its fields by name), enum; plus the object's one word, from. A field the base already declares appears here only to be re-briefed: description alone. No default, no preview: an object is a kind, never an instance.

type.description: JSON Schema's word, or unoverse-markdown for a body (UNOVERSE_AUTHORING 3b). Omitted on a re-brief of an inherited field.

input.description: true: the model writes it from the source. false: the engine or the function writes it (from: names which). Explicit on every prop the object declares itself.

description.description: THE BRIEF. The whole instruction for this field; a stranger could fill it from this alone. May name the org's identity: {{ identity.<document>.<field> }}.

from.description: <function>.<return> of api/service.yaml: the made detail this prop is written from (README 4b). Absent: written from the thin item.

hydrate.description: How a component fills this field from the row (UNOVERSE_AUTHORING 3b): image, link, icon.

answeredBy.description: The kinds of document that may answer this field (the reading document's choice, e.g. offering-memorandum). Each page of a document of one of these kinds is asked for the field while it is still empty, and a value stated is written with its page and words (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/proved-before-built.md). On an object filled from documents, every input: true field names them.

standard.description: The field's id in the org's field list (one org's list is openfunds: OFST452010). A table's column or row named by this field's wordings, or by the standard field's own name, fills it (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/tables.md).

format.description: date: the field is a date, written yyyy-mm-dd. A date a document prints another way (31/Mar/2025, 21 October 2024) is written so; one that could be read two ways (03/04/2025) is left, never guessed. country: the field is a country, held by its one name from ISO 3166-1 (its code named by the CLDR English region names) however a document prints it (UK, GB and United Kingdom are United Kingdom); a value no country fits stays as printed.

pattern.description: The regular expression a value must match (an ISIN: ^[A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]{9}[0-9]$). A value that does not match is never saved, whichever reader read it.

wordings.description: The words documents print for this field (management related fees, mgmt fee), matched exactly after lower case. A new wording is proposed, approved by a person, then added here (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/tables.md).

wordingsIn.description: Words that name this field in one kind of document only, as { <document type>: [<words>] }, where one type prints for this field the words another prints for another field (an offering document's management fee is its maximum). The scoped words win over the plain wordings for that type.

onlyWith.description: Another field of this object that this one is a term of; where a record states that field as none, this one is not kept (a hurdle only with a performance fee).

none.description: The value a table cell that states there is none ("None", "N/A", "-", "Nil") stands for (0 for a fee), kept as stated; without it such a cell fills nothing. Never a default: a field the documents do not state stays empty.

reuse.description: true: the read is shown the values this field already holds on the object's rows in the org, and gives one of them, spelled exactly, when it names the same thing. For a name many rows share: a subject, a series.

oneOf.description: A choice's options, each its stored word, what a person reads and how the model tells it apart (docs/unoverse/data/objects/README.md 4c). Never with enum.

description.description: The brief for this field of the element.

field.description: One field of an element, in the prop grammar one level down: no input (the array's says who writes it), no from.

description.description: The brief for this field of the element.

scalar.description: An array of scalars: the element's type and its limits.

items.description: The shape of one element (README 4c: the same grammar one level down): { type: string, maxLength } for a scalar, or the element's fields by name, each a brief.
